gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the three picks' reach on the same basis. At 4K60 they are OREI UHD12-EX115-K 115 ft (Cat6 or better), J-Tech JTECH-14EX60-AE 196–197 ft (J-Tech says Cat5e/6 works) and OREI UHD14-EXB400-K 394 ft (HDBaseT, Cat6 or better). All three share the same 18 Gbps ceiling, so J-Tech's 196 ft at 4K60 claim is 70% longer than OREI's at the same bandwidth, while OREI rates its own 1x2 for about 197 ft only at 1080p.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited OREI pages (UHD12-EX115-K and UHD14-EXB400-K Overview and Use Cases). Each gives distance by resolution for its own OREI unit only: 115/164/197 ft and 394/492 ft. Neither mentions J-Tech. None of the 12 OREI support results compares brands or points out that ChatGPT's '4K60 · 196 ft' card for J-Tech and '4K60 · 115 ft' card for OREI are rated on different terms: different cable grades, and the same 18 Gbps for both. So the rivals have part of the table (OREI's rows) but not the cross-brand footnote.
decides: 4K60 at up to about 115 ft (35 m): any of the three is rated for it, and the cheapest that matches the number of TVs wins (OREI UHD12-EX115-K for 2 TVs). From 115 ft to 196 ft: only J-Tech's own claim covers it. J-Tech says that over Cat5e/6 with an 18 Gbps maximum, the same budget for which OREI promises only 115 ft at 4K60 and 197 ft at 1080p. Treat it as unproven, and J-Tech's own store showed it unavailable on 2026-11-13. Past 196 ft, or wherever 4K60 has to work first time: OREI UHD14-EXB400-K (HDBaseT, 394 ft at 4K60) is the only pick rated for it, so the long-run HDBaseT pick is confirmed and J-Tech's spot as 'best overall 1×4' gets weaker.
